---
title: "Negative binomial models"
description: "Sparse regression for overdispersed counts with NB1 or NB2 variance."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
library(L0glm)
options(width=90, digits=3)
```

For overdispersed counts the NB2 model has

\[
E(Y_i)=\mu_i,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(Y_i)=\mu_i+\mu_i^2/\theta.
\]

The Poisson limit is approached as `theta` increases. `mgcv::nb()` estimates
theta alongside the coefficients; `mgcv::nb(theta=2)` keeps it fixed.
The default link is log.

## NB2 with fixed or estimated shape

```{r fit}
set.seed(21)
X <- matrix(rnorm(350*20), 350, 20)
mu <- exp(.4 + X[, 2] - .8*X[, 7])
y <- rnbinom(350, mu=mu, size=2)
fit <- l0glmFit(X, y, family=mgcv::nb(), intercept=TRUE,
  lambda="gic", maxit=100, tol=1e-8)
fit
fit$theta
predict(fit, X[1:5, ], type="response")
fixed <- l0glmFit(X, y, family=mgcv::nb(theta=2), intercept=TRUE,
  lambda="gic")
coef(fixed)[c(1, 3, 8), , drop=FALSE]
```

For multichannel counts, supply an observation-by-channel matrix. `grouped=TRUE`
selects predictor rows jointly. A criterion-checked support refit can refine
eligible coefficients in the selected rows. Shapes may be estimated separately by channel.

## NB1 with a constant variance-to-mean ratio

Use `nb1(dispersion=phi)` when the variance grows in proportion to the mean,
\(\operatorname{Var}(Y_i)=\phi\mu_i\), for a supplied \(\phi\ge 1\). With
\(\phi>1\), the equivalent negative binomial size for observation \(i\) is
\(\mu_i/(\phi-1)\). At \(\phi=1\), the family reduces to Poisson.

```{r nb1}
phi <- 2
y1 <- rnbinom(nrow(X), mu=mu, size=mu/(phi - 1))
fit1 <- l0glmFit(X, y1, family=nb1(dispersion=phi), intercept=TRUE,
  lambda="gic")
predict(fit1, X[1:5, ], type="response")
```

## Tune by GIC or CV

```{r tuning, eval=FALSE}
gic <- l0glmTune(X, y, family=mgcv::nb(), intercept=TRUE,
  tune="gic", nlambda=10, maxit=100)
cv <- l0glmTune(X, y, family=mgcv::nb(), intercept=TRUE,
  tune="cv", nfolds=5, nlambda=10, maxit=100)
predict(cv$fit_1se, X[1:5, ])
```

Each training fold estimates its own theta. Observation weights and offsets
are supported. The [negative-binomial reference](../reference/L0glm_negative_binomial.html)
details the likelihood and shape updates. The family convention follows
[`mgcv::nb()`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/mgcv/html/negbin.html).
